title: Comparison of personalized hemodynamic management with pulse‑pressure‑variation–guided fluid therapy and standard therapy in elective neurosurgical tumor resections
summary: During surgeries for the removal of brain tumors, maintaining stable circulatory conditions is essential to preserve cerebral perfusion and prevent complications. Circulatory and fluid management in brain tumor surgery is particularly distinctive because osmotic diuretics are administered to shrink the brain and improve the surgeon’s view. This study compares three different strategies for guiding circulatory and fluid therapy during brain tumor surgery. The aim is to determine whether an individually tailored hemodynamic therapy leads to better circulatory stability and fewer complications than the currently standard treatment or management based on pulse pressure variation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective intracranial tumor resection.
Written informed consent obtained prior to study participation.
Exclusion criteria:
- Chronic kidney disease (estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m²) 
- acute kidney injury (KDIGO stage ≥ C1)
- Impaired left ventricular systolic function (left ventricular ejection fraction <35%)
- Right ventricular dysfunction
- Intracardiac shunt
- Permanent cardiac arrhythmias
- Heart rate to respiratory rate ratio <3.6 
- aortic valve stenosis (valve area <1 cm² or mean pressure gradient >40 mmHg)
- Acute myocardial ischemia within 30 days prior to randomization
- Peripheral arterial occlusive disease (Fontaine stage ≥IIb)
- Respiratory system compliance <30 mL/cmH₂O
- Preoperative hemoglobin concentration <10 g/dL
- Inability to obtain a reliable preoperative baseline cardiac index because of inadequate echocardiographic image quality (Ultrasound befor randomization)
